summary: Khushiyon Ki Chaabi, Mera Godrej Ghar celebrates the joy of a place to call your own. From receiving the keys to lighting the first diya, discover ways to welcome your family, honour your traditions and make your first Diwali in a Godrej home a beginning to remember.

sections.markdown:
A key opens a door. The moments that follow make it home: the first family visit, a familiar voice in a new room, and a diya lit at the entrance on Diwali evening.

**Khushiyon Ki Chaabi, Mera Godrej Ghar** brings that feeling to the heart of the festive season. It is about the happiness of belonging, the people you share a home with, and the everyday memories waiting to be made.

Every family's homecoming has its own rhythm. Receiving the keys, celebrating Diwali and holding a formal housewarming need not happen on the same day. You can plan these milestones around your family's traditions, the readiness of your home and advice from your priest.

Here is a guide to making those first celebrations thoughtful and personal, from the joy of key handover to welcoming light, loved ones and new beginnings into your Godrej home.

sections.title: 1. A new beginning, at a time that feels right
sections.question: Is it good to do griha pravesh during Diwali?
sections.answer: Families observing Chaturmas commonly defer formal griha pravesh until a suitable muhurat afterwards; confirm your family's practice with your priest.
sections.markdown:
**Short answer: usually not, and the reason is Chaturmas rather than Diwali itself.**

Diwali almost always falls within Chaturmas, the four-month period beginning at
Devshayani Ekadashi and ending at Dev Uthani Ekadashi, during which Lord Vishnu is
believed to rest. Many families avoid housewarming ceremonies, weddings and other
major auspicious beginnings during this window.

In 2026, Diwali fell on 8 November and Chaturmas ended at Dev Uthani Ekadashi on
20 November. A family taking possession during Diwali week was therefore inside
Chaturmas, which is why a priest would commonly have advised holding the formal
ceremony until after the 20th.

This does not mean the Diwali period is inauspicious. It means griha pravesh, as a
formal Vedic ceremony, is traditionally kept for a muhurat outside Chaturmas. Moving
in, cleaning, lighting diyas and celebrating are a separate matter, covered in
section 6.

Practice varies by region and by family. Some communities observe Chaturmas
strictly, others only partially. Your family priest is the authority on which
applies to you.

sections.title: 2. Planning your homecoming around family traditions
sections.question: Which months should we avoid for griha pravesh?
sections.answer: Many families avoid Chaturmas and Kharmas or Dhanurmasam for griha pravesh, but the applicable periods depend on regional and family traditions.
sections.markdown:
Chaturmas runs for roughly four lunar months through the monsoon. The practical
tradition behind it is straightforward: travel, construction and large gatherings
were historically difficult during the rains, so major ceremonies were deferred.

Two further periods are commonly avoided for griha pravesh:

| Period | Dates | What families usually do |
|---|---|---|
| Chaturmas | Ends at Dev Uthani Ekadashi, 20 November 2026 | Formal griha pravesh is deferred until after it ends |
| Kharmas / Dhanurmasam | 16 December 2026 to 14 January 2027 | Many Telugu, Tamil and North Indian families keep this month for dawn worship rather than housewarmings |
| Adhik Maas and Ashada | Varies by year | Several regional traditions avoid housewarming entirely |

Note that panchang listings will still show technically valid muhurats inside these
windows, because the calculation method and family custom are two different things.
A date can be astrologically clear and still be one your family would not use.

sections.title: 3. The joy of receiving your keys
sections.question: Is Dhanteras a good day to get the keys?
sections.answer: Dhanteras is traditionally considered auspicious for receiving a home's keys, but key handover is separate from moving in or performing griha pravesh.
sections.markdown:
**Short answer: yes, Dhanteras is considered an auspicious day to receive your keys,
and this is distinct from griha pravesh.**

Dhanteras marks the worship of Dhanvantari and, by extension, the acquisition of
things of lasting value. This is why families traditionally buy gold, silver and
utensils on this day. Taking possession of a home, receiving the keys, and
completing registration formalities all sit comfortably within that tradition.

What Dhanteras does not require is that you move in or perform the ceremony that day.

A common and entirely traditional sequence looks like this:

- **Dhanteras:** collect the keys, complete handover formalities, carry in a small
  symbolic item such as a silver coin, a vessel or a lamp
- **Diwali:** clean the home, light diyas at the threshold, perform Lakshmi puja
- **After Dev Uthani Ekadashi:** perform the formal griha pravesh on a chosen muhurat,
  then begin living in the home

This sequence lets a family mark Diwali in the new home without compromising the
ceremony.

sections.title: 4. Lakshmi puja before or after griha pravesh
sections.question: Lakshmi puja before or after griha pravesh?
sections.answer: Diwali Lakshmi puja can precede griha pravesh, while the Lakshmi invocation within the housewarming ceremony takes place on its chosen muhurat, subject to family tradition.
sections.markdown:
**Short answer: Diwali Lakshmi puja can be performed in a home before griha pravesh.
The Lakshmi puja that forms part of the griha pravesh ritual is a separate, later
observance.**

These are two different pujas that share a name, which is the source of most of the
confusion.

**Diwali Lakshmi puja** is an annual festival observance tied to the calendar. It is
performed wherever the family is on Diwali night. If you have possession of a new
home and wish to light it that evening, you may perform Diwali Lakshmi puja there.

**Griha pravesh Lakshmi puja** is part of the housewarming ritual sequence, performed
on the chosen muhurat, usually alongside Ganesh puja, Vastu Shanti and the boiling
over of milk. It marks the formal consecration of the home.

The conventional order is Ganesh puja first, then Vastu Shanti, then Lakshmi
invocation, then the milk ceremony, then the first meal cooked in the home. Regional
practice varies, and your priest will set the order appropriate to your tradition.

sections.title: 5. Griha pravesh muhurat dates: November 2026 to March 2027
sections.question: How should we choose a griha pravesh muhurat between November 2026 and March 2027?
sections.answer: Confirm any proposed griha pravesh date and time against a location-specific panchang and your family's traditions before booking the ceremony.
sections.markdown:
These dates are drawn from standard panchang calculations for New Delhi and
Hyderabad. Time windows vary by city, so confirm the exact muhurat with a priest or
a panchang set to your location.

| Month | Auspicious dates |
|---|---|
| November 2026 | 11, 14, 20, 21, 25, 26 |
| December 2026 | 2, 3, 4, 11, 12, 18, 19, 30 |
| January 2027 | 1 |
| February 2027 | 10, 11, 15, 22, 24, 25, 27 |
| March 2027 | 3, 4, 10, 11, 15, 22, 24, 26, 27, 31 |

Points worth noting:

- **The gap from 2 January to 9 February 2027** is not an oversight. Those days are
  ruled out on nakshatra, weekday or tithi, and the lunar month from 8 January to
  6 February is itself considered unfavourable for entering a new home.
- **The 18, 19 and 30 December dates and 1 January** fall inside Kharmas. They are
  astrologically valid but many families avoid them.
- **Uttarayana**, roughly January to June, is traditionally regarded as the stronger
  half of the year for housewarming.
- **Pushya, Rohini, Shravana and Anuradha** nakshatras are considered the most
  favourable. Tuesdays and Saturdays, and the tithis of Ekadashi, Purnima and
  Amavasya, are generally avoided.
- If no suitable muhurat is available, **Abhijit muhurat**, the short window around
  solar noon, is the traditional fallback.

sections.title: 6. Your first Diwali in your Godrej home
sections.question: Can we celebrate our first Diwali before griha pravesh?
sections.answer: Many families celebrate Diwali in their new home before formal griha pravesh, while observing their family's customs and the building's fire-safety rules.
sections.markdown:
A home does not need to be formally consecrated to be celebrated in.

If you have your keys but your griha pravesh muhurat falls later, there is a long
tradition of marking the home gently in the interim:

- Light diyas at the threshold and on the balcony
- Draw a rangoli at the entrance
- Hang a toran at the main door
- Perform Diwali Lakshmi puja
- Share a meal, even a simple one, with family in the space
- Bring in a symbolic first item: a lamp, a vessel, a plant, a photograph

What is usually deferred until after griha pravesh is permanent residence, moving the
household in fully, and the formal consecration rituals.

For most families the first Diwali in a new home is remembered less for the ceremony
than for the evening itself. The campaign film closes on exactly this moment, a
couple celebrating their first Diwali in a home that is finally theirs.

faqs.question: Is it good to do griha pravesh during Diwali?
faqs.answer: Usually not, though the reason is Chaturmas rather than Diwali itself. Diwali typically falls within Chaturmas, the four-month period when major auspicious ceremonies are traditionally deferred. In 2026 Chaturmas ended on 20 November, twelve days after Diwali. Receiving keys and celebrating in the home during Diwali is customary; the formal ceremony is generally kept for a muhurat afterwards.

faqs.question: Is Dhanteras a good day to get the keys?
faqs.answer: Yes. Dhanteras is traditionally associated with acquiring things of lasting value, which is why gold, silver and utensils are bought that day. Taking possession of a home, completing handover formalities and carrying in a symbolic first item all fit that tradition. It does not require that you move in or perform griha pravesh the same day.

faqs.question: Can we celebrate our first Diwali before griha pravesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lighting diyas, drawing a rangoli, hanging a toran, performing Diwali Lakshmi puja and sharing a meal in the home are all customary before formal consecration. What is usually deferred is permanent residence and the griha pravesh rituals themselves.

faqs.question: Lakshmi puja before or after griha pravesh?
faqs.answer: Both, because they are two different pujas. Diwali Lakshmi puja is an annual festival observance and can be performed in the home before griha pravesh. The Lakshmi invocation within the griha pravesh sequence is separate and happens on the chosen muhurat.

faqs.question: Is it auspicious to move in during Diwali week?
faqs.answer: Taking possession is widely considered auspicious during Diwali week, particularly on Dhanteras. Moving in fully is a different question, and in most years Diwali week falls inside Chaturmas, so families commonly wait for a muhurat afterwards. Regional practice varies.

faqs.question: What is the right way to do griha pravesh around Diwali?
faqs.answer: The common sequence is: collect keys on Dhanteras, celebrate Diwali in the home with diyas and Lakshmi puja, then perform the formal griha pravesh on a muhurat after Dev Uthani Ekadashi. The ceremony itself usually runs Ganesh puja, Vastu Shanti, Lakshmi invocation, the boiling over of milk, and the first meal cooked in the home.

faqs.question: Which months should we avoid for griha pravesh?
faqs.answer: Chaturmas, which ended on 20 November 2026, and Kharmas or Dhanurmasam, 16 December 2026 to 14 January 2027, are the two main periods. The lunar month from 8 January to 6 February 2027 is also considered unfavourable. Several regional traditions additionally avoid Adhik Maas and Ashada.

faqs.question: Do we need a priest for griha pravesh?
faqs.answer: Most families engage one, since the ritual sequence and the muhurat calculation are both traditionally his role. Simpler observances performed by the family alone are also common, particularly for apartments and for second homes.

faqs.question: What should we carry into the new home first?
faqs.answer: Customs vary. Commonly a lit lamp, a vessel of water, a kalash, grain or a silver coin, carried in by the senior-most woman of the family. Some traditions lead with a cow, which is rarely practical in an apartment, so the lamp or kalash is the usual substitute.

faqs.question: Can griha pravesh be done in an apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes. The full ritual sequence adapts to apartments without difficulty. The milk ceremony, the threshold rangoli and the first meal all work in a flat. Where a traditional step requires outdoor space, a balcony or the apartment entrance is the accepted substitute.
